test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 25th November 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The average weight of some persons in a group is 70 kg. When 15 persons with average weight 60 kg leave the group or 15 persons with average weight 87.5 kg join the group, then the average weight of persons in the group in both the cases is equal. How many persons were there in the group, initially?
solution:
Given:

The average weight of some persons in a group is 70 kg. 

When 15 persons with an average weight of 60 kg leave the group or 15 persons with an average weight of 87.5 kg join the group, then the average weight of persons in the group in both cases is equal.

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

Calculation:

Let the number of persons in the group be N.

Initially total weight of the persons in the group = 70N

According to the question,

(70N + 15 × 87.5)/(N + 15) = (70N - 15 × 60)/(N - 15)

⇒ (N + 15)/(N - 15) = (70N + 1312.5)/(70N - 900)

Applying the Componendo-Dividendo method,

⇒ (N + 15 + N - 15)/(N + 15 - N + 15) = (70N + 1312.5 + 70N - 900)/(70N + 1312.5 - 70N + 900)

⇒ 2N/30 = (140N + 412.5)/2212.5

⇒ N/15 = (140N + 412.5)/2212.5

⇒ N = (140N + 412.5)/147.5

⇒ 147.5N = 140N + 412.5

⇒ 7.5N = 412.5

⇒ N = 412.5/7.5

⇒ N = 55

∴ 55 persons were there in the group initially.
